subject: Throughput ladder upsell and rate-tier alignment
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
To: Dana Cole <dana@flowline.ai>
Cc: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
Date: 2027-10-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Throughput ladder proposal — staged uplift + rate-tier map

Hi Dana,

Thanks again for the time on Friday — big thanks to your ML infra team for the usage breakdown. I pulled together a short proposal for a staged commit uplift that aims to keep your unit cost steady while giving you headroom for the expected Fall campaign.

Key idea (high level):
- Month 1–3: soft-step increase to a 2x monthly commit (auto burst pocket retained) to absorb campaign spikes.
- Month 4–6: move to a commitment ladder (3 tiers) that reduces per-token rate as aggregate commit grows.
- Add a small monthly softcap credit to smooth over forecasting errors.

Attachments: Flowline-Monthly-Usage.csv (your 6-month token profile). I also sketched a sample amendment (high level) — if this approach sounds right I’ll get legal to draft a formal addendum.

Quick asks: can procurement share the target monthly commit range they can commit to (ballpark), and any internal SLA or data-retention constraints we should bake in?

If you prefer a quick 30-min to walk the numbers, I can do Wed or Thu next week.

Thanks,
Marcus
Account Executive — Enterprise 
Redwood Inference

--
Attachment: Flowline-Monthly-Usage.csv (CSV, 42 KB)
From: Dana Cole <dana@flowline.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-10-02T11:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Throughput ladder proposal — staged uplift + rate-tier map

Marcus,

Appreciate the proposal and the CSV — the team validated the numbers this morning. High level, Flowline is interested in the ladder approach. A few notes from our side:
- Procurement is looking at a 90–120 day commitment window initially; likely able to commit to ~1.8–2.2x current monthly for the first quarter.
- We need a clear fallback if usage drops below committed baseline (how credits/overage are handled).
- Can you confirm how the burst pocket interacts with the ladder (is it separate billing bucket or nested)?

Looping in procurement (procurement@flowline.ai) for the contract-side questions. Procurement will want the draft terms and a sample invoice cadence.

Also cc'ing our head of infra (helena@flowline.ai) for any technical constraints.

Can you put together a short one-pager with: proposed tiers, per-token rates at each tier, burst handling, and a sample invoice for month 1 vs month 4? If you can get that over by Thursday we can route internally.

Thanks,
Dana
Head of Product
Flowline.ai
From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: 2027-10-03T08:23:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Flowline interest — need pricing one-pager + amendment stub

Folks — forwarding Dana's reply. Procurement asked for: tiers, per-token rates, burst rules, and a sample invoice. They can commit ~1.8–2.2x for Q1; goal is to move them up ladder by month 4.

My proposed plan:
1) Create a one-page rate table with three tiers: Base (current commit x1), Ladder-1 (x2), Ladder-2 (x3). Show per-token delta and total monthly invoice examples (current vs month1 vs month4).
2) Document burst pocket semantics: keep a separate monthly burst allowance (billed at burst rate) with a small monthly carryover credit if unused.
3) Draft a short amendment (2 pages) that includes: effective dates, ladder thresholds, invoice cadence, and overage/fallback language. Legal can convert it to full contract wording.

Vanessa — can you run the rate calc with the usage CSV and return a clean table? Karh tik — can you confirm whether we need any special SLA language for Flowline's infra constraints (they mentioned retention & fallback)? Lauren — want you to own the amendment stub + DocuSign link creation.

I'm aiming to have the one-pager and amendment draft to send to Dana by Monday (10/4 EOD PST).

Thanks,
Marcus

From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>

Cc: Flowline Procurement <procurement@flowline.ai>, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: 2027-10-04T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Proposed ladder amendment & sample invoice (next steps)

Hi Dana — looping back with the one-pager and next steps.

Summary (short):
- Q1 (months 1–3): soft-step commit at 2x current monthly (commit band = 2.0x). Per-token rate for Q1 = $0.00115 (example). Burst pocket: 15% of baseline, billed separately at $0.0018/token; unused burst converts to a $500 monthly credit up to 2 months.
- Months 4–6: Ladder applies (Tier A = 2x, Tier B = 3x, Tier C = 4x). Effective per-token rates drop by ~12% at each ladder step.
- Fallback & overage: if actual monthly usage < 90% of committed baseline for two consecutive months, credits will be reconciled and a one-time catch-up invoice may apply; we included a 30-day notice window for customer opt-down.

Attachments: Draft-Amendment-terms.pdf (clean stub). I also uploaded the one-pager to the HubSpot deal (link below).

Next steps:
1) Review the attached amendment stub with procurement and confirm the target commit band (you indicated 1.8–2.2x). If 2.0x works, I'll push the DocuSign for signature.
2) If procurement wants tighter fallback language, let us know the exact recovery mechanics and we'll loop legal.
3) Quick sync — I propose a 20-min call tomorrow 9:00 AM PT to walk the invoice examples and get signoff.

Links: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/flowline/5412 — Draft and one-pager are attached to the deal. DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/en/documents/FL-5412-amendment (will be live once procurement confirms commit).

Thanks — happy to adjust the rates if procurement has a different target commit.

Best,
Marcus
Account Executive — Enterprise
Redwood Inference
